policy.decision: Person Domain v2 Review Unit 03. Reclassify one bounded 12-Person philosophy/religion slice from legacy knowledge. Every write requires live Production previous_domain=knowledge; any drift fails closed.

review_scope.selection_rule: Complete all nine Japan philosophy-canon records from batch-104 and all three India Buddhist philosophy records from batch-105 as one 12-Person bounded v2 review unit.

entries.basis: V2 religion covers religious leadership and faith traditions. Dōgen founded the Japanese Sōtō Zen tradition and organized a distinctive religious practice centered on zazen; institutional religious leadership is stronger than generic philosophical classification.

V2 religion covers founders and religious reformers. Hōnen established the Pure Land movement that became a distinct Japanese religious tradition; his representative identity is sect-forming religious leadership.

V2 religion covers religious founders and institutional traditions. Kūkai is most famous as founder of Japanese Shingon esoteric Buddhism and established its doctrine, ritual system, and monastic center; this outweighs his many literary and technical accomplishments.

V2 culture covers humanities, philology, literature, and philosophy. Norinaga is represented by Kokugaku philology, interpretation of ancient Japanese texts, literary thought, and Shintō philosophy rather than institutional religious leadership.

V2 religion covers founders and religious reformers. Nichiren created the Nichiren school and a distinctive Lotus Sutra-centered religious movement; sect founding is the representative historical identity.

V2 culture covers philosophy and humanities. Nishida is explicitly treated as a major twentieth-century Japanese philosopher and founder of an original philosophical system; Buddhist influence does not make him primarily a religious leader.
V2 culture covers philosophy, humanities, and social thought. Sorai is represented by Confucian philosophical, philological, ethical, and political thought rather than by exercising political office.
V2 religion covers founders and institutional religious traditions. Saichō founded Japanese Tendai and established the school that became a major monastic and religious institution.

V2 religion covers religious leadership and enduring faith traditions. Shinran's Pure Land teaching became the basis of Jōdo Shinshū and his representative identity is religious teacher and tradition-forming reformer.

V2 culture covers philosophy and humanities. Dignāga is a pivotal philosopher of logic and epistemology in classical India; his representative work concerns reasoning, inference, and argument rather than natural science or religious institution-building.

V2 culture covers philosophy. Nāgārjuna is canonically described as one of the most important Buddhist philosophers and founder of a major philosophical system; monastic status does not outweigh his philosophical representative identity.

V2 culture covers philosophy and humanities. Vasubandhu is represented by Buddhist philosophical analysis, especially Yogācāra and Abhidharma thought; this is intellectual-philosophical rather than natural science or institutional religious leadership.
